A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPSE research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic cycle-counting experiments, retrained graph-benchmark comparisons, and path-count sensitivity measurements in Section 5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and results in Section 5, with supporting configurations and examples in the appendices.

M1.justification: The DAG decomposition, DFS/partial-BFS/BFS procedure, maximum-count update, logarithmic encoding, and model integrations are unchanged. v2's explicit maximum-update explanation already appears in v1's Section 5.4 and Algorithm 3; accommodating exact counts is a clarification, not a demonstrated procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic cycle-counting task and eight benchmarks spanning molecular, SBM, and superpixel graphs. The added comparator introduces no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GPS+GPSE comparisons on ZINC, Peptides-functional, Peptides-structural, MNIST, and CIFAR10. Its caption explicitly identifies these as results from a model that was not retrained. All existing comparator methods remain.

E3.justification: The retained experiments use unchanged reported splits, metrics, model configurations, training budgets, and numerical path-count settings. Appendix A expands documentation of parameter selection without establishing changed settings or reruns; GPS+GPSE is a separately sourced comparison.

E4.justification: The hyperparameter sensitivity study in Section 5.3, approximate-count failure example in Section 5.4, and synthetic graph examples are retained unchanged. The added expressivity discussion does not introduce an empirical ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions already report ten random-seed runs, one run for PCQM4Mv2, standard deviations, and two-sided Student's t-tests with p-value threshold 0.05. Changes to individual reported deviations do not change these practices.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds five GPS+GPSE scores and changes CSA-SPSE Peptides-structural MAE from 0.24945 ± 0.0018 to 0.2482 ± 0.0019, reversing its comparison with CSA-RWSE without a significance marker. Table 2 revises ZINC density from 0.09 to 0.10 and Peptides density from 0.27 to 0.03. The retained '21 out of 24' summary now conflicts with 22 improvements in Table 1.

T1.justification: New Appendix B adds theoretical assertions about SPSE attention exceeding 1-WL and retaining GRIT expressivity properties except Proposition 3.1(b). It also explains why existing path-tree proofs do not establish an SPSE-versus-RWSE ordering. No complete new proof is supplied; Propositions 1–3 and their proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The conclusion drops v1's general 'more expressive' characterization while retaining greater structural informativeness, consistent with the new qualification that a general SPSE-versus-RWSE expressivity comparison remains open. The principal method, local cycle-information, and empirical-performance claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes local edge informativeness from unresolved graph-isomorphism expressivity ordering. Section 5.4 newly suggests preferring exact shorter-path counts when approximation harms performance, and the conclusion proposes hierarchical path mining. These qualify and extend interpretation without adding supporting experiments.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly describes the tabulated alpha, beta, and n values as yielding the best dataset results and explains their compression and scaling roles. Their numerical values, reported computation times, detailed algorithm, and repository destination are unchanged. This disclosure is not reconciled with Section 5.2's retained no-tuning statement.

R1.justification: v2 adds Cantürk et al.'s GPSE work and more precisely positions SPSE against Path-WL, path-based GNNs, and GRIT in Appendix B. Other bibliography changes largely update or consolidate existing works rather than introduce new research coverage.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized explanatory edits, expands Appendix A, inserts an expressivity appendix and acknowledgments, and adjusts subsequent appendix references. The main section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The document-wide transition to ICML formatting changes the title and abstract arrangement, typography, headers, captions, and float placement. Figure 7 moves onto a dedicated page, and Table 1 gains a comparator row and explanatory note. All eight figure graphics themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves scientific qualification by explicitly separating local structural advantages from an unproved general expressivity ordering. The GPSE comparison and expanded parameter explanation provide useful context. These are limited gains: the experimental foundation is largely unchanged, the revised Table 1 leaves an outdated improvement count, and Appendix A's best-result parameter selection remains in tension with the no-tuning claim.
